FINAL RESULT (amended per your single fix — directional modifiers removed; nothing else changed)

REQUESTED TABLE — habitat-level covariate medians, sorted by %gard (all 10 habitats):
habitat | elev_med(m) | urban500m_med | cropland1000m_med | occurrences | %gard
Broad-leaved forests* | 639.5 | 0.010 | 0.050 | 4 | 100.0
Coniferous forests | 591.0 | 0.010 | 0.090 | 8 | 87.5
Wetlands | 147.5 | 0.125 | 0.175 | 52 | 55.8
Coastal | 10.0 | 0.070 | 0.250 | 43 | 53.5

Rock outcrops* | 990.0 | 0.000 | 0.050 | 1 | 0.0
(* descriptive-only per rare-cell rule)

VERDICT ON DIRECTIONAL CLAIMS — NOT CONFIRMED, so elevation/urban modifiers are removed from the hypothesis:
- Forests do sit at 591–640 m with urban500 median 0.01, but Meadows (896 m, 0.01) and Rock outcrops (990 m, 0.00) are equally "high/minimal-urban" yet unintentional-leaning — the covariates do not discriminate the forests' gardening dominance.
- Croplands have median urban500 = 0.05 (low, not "high urban cover"); only habitat-internal cropland cover (0.325) is high, which is tautological for the Croplands class.
- "Meadows/riparian intermediate on the same gradient" fails outright: meadows are the highest-elevation, lowest-urban tested habitat yet have the second-lowest gardening share among natural habitats.
This is exactly the non-monotonicity already shown (|rho| ≤ 0.2); the claim is therefore purely categorical.

FINAL HYPOTHESIS (categorical context, no unsupported directions):
The gardening pathway for introducing non-native plants shows two prevalence styles structured by habitat land-use category, not by elevation or urban-cover gradients. In managed/developed habitats — croplands and urban areas, with meadows and riparian zones leaning the same way — unintentional introductions dominate (69–77% of species occurrences in croplands/urban) and gardening is a minority (19–31%). In semi-natural habitats — coniferous and broad-leaved forests, and hydromorphic wetlands and coastal habitats — gardening is dominant or co-dominant (54–100% of occurrences). Habitat type and pathway are significantly associated (habitat × pathway contingency on 476 species occurrences: chi2 = 67.11, df = 14, Monte-Carlo p = 0.0002, Cramér's V = 0.266), while continuous context covariates (median elevation, urban.2009.500m, cropland.2009.1000m) show no monotonic habitat-level relationship (all |rho| ≤ 0.2, descriptive n = 10) — e.g., wetlands and coastal combine high gardening share with low elevation and low-to-moderate urban cover, and meadows combine low gardening share with high elevation and minimal urban cover. Context, in short, is habitat naturalness/land-use category: gardening-introduced species shift from minority escapees in intensively used habitats to the majority of non-native records in semi-natural plant communities, against the temporal backdrop of gardening rising to 75% of introductions after 1985. Caveats: occurrence-based counts (multi-habitat species counted per habitat) and a regional species pool already 52% gardening, so shares partly reflect pool composition; no introduction-vs-establishment decomposition claimed.

LOW-N CONFIRMATION (your question): Coniferous forests (8 occ.) and Scrublands (5) were deliberately kept in the main test — they are above the pre-declared row-total < 5 threshold, and excluding them changes nothing qualitatively (recomputed as a check: 6-habitat test N = 463, chi2 = 55.07, df = 10, MC p = 0.0001, V = 0.244 — same significance and same conclusion; their contrast signs, Coniferous +87.5pp gardening-leaning and Scrublands −20.0pp unintentional-leaning, are consistent with the reported grouping). Note this is a robustness check beyond the approved scope, computed only to answer your question.

UNCHANGED FROM APPROVED CORE: test (chi2 = 67.11, df = 14, MC p = 0.0002, V = 0.266), contrast table, rules R1–R5 (AgriForest→Other; row-total <5 → descriptive-only for Broad-leaved (4) and Rock outcrops (1); 441 zero-count plots untouched), caveats.

payload.workflow: 1) Inspected all four staged inputs (TSV formats; no NA/duplicates; additivity n.gard+n.unint+n.agfo==n.total on 632/632 rows; pathway labels cross-checked against invasion_success_pathways.csv; pool = 51.9% gardening). 2) Habitat x pathway species-occurrence table (10 habitats). 3) Pre-declared rules: AgriForest(23)->Other; habitats with row total <5 (Broad-leaved forests 4, Rock outcrops 1) descriptive-only, excluded from test; 441 zero-count plots retained (contribute 0 occurrences). 4) Main test: habitat(8) x pathway(3) chi-square, 10,000 fixed-margin Monte-Carlo p (min expected 0.24), Cramér's V. 5) Secondary contrast: gardening vs unintentional % shares per habitat with signed contrast. 6) Context covariates elevation + urban.2009.500m (500 m intermediate buffer), habitat-level Spearman marked descriptive (n=10/n=8), plus one sensitivity line (cropland.2009.1000m, annual.temperature). 7) Amendment step: habitat-level medians of elevation/urban.2009.500m/cropland.2009.1000m for all 10 habitats sorted by %gard showed directional elevation/urban claims unsupported (Meadows high elevation/low urban but low gardening; Croplands low urban median) -> hypothesis restated as purely categorical. 8) Low-N robustness check excluding Coniferous forests (8) and Scrublands (5): chi2=55.07, df=10, MC p=0.0001, V=0.244 — conclusion unchanged. No phylogenetics, no temporal analysis beyond framing line, no species x habitat reconstruction.
